post.0:
I finished third on 87, fifteen behind Ben, and I lost it in round II: Cal took the blue lead off Polisher-into-Bury, then answered my Polish with Peek, and I ended the round holding no contest at all, so I went into round III with nothing to fight for but conversion. My blue engine (Trendsetters plus Bargain Bin, then Connoisseurs, Snobs, Critic and Regular off one Spree) was really efficient; Snobs alone paid 13 at game end, so the patient plan wasn't the problem. The problem was that every big swing on the table came from cashing out expensive cards or center spaces (Heiresses into Farewell, Cash In with Brokers, Largesse, Extra Hand into Farewell), and my cheap members can't keep pace with that. The decisive moment was Ben's Last Call finish: Party Crasher onto Largesse for +10 and Extra Hand straight into Farewell for 9, five unanswerable placements after everyone else was done. Even Ben's Largesse handing me 10 silver to tie silver didn't close the gap.

META: The contests and the snake are working: every round had real reads about who could still reach a color, and denying spaces mattered. What isn't working is that cash-out spaces scale with card cost (Farewell, Bury, Estate Sale) and center spaces (Largesse, Cash In) are so large that cheap-member engines can't keep up, and Last Call plus Party Crasher lets one player take the last five actions of the game unanswered. First change: make Farewell pay printed followers or half cost instead of full cost, and stop Party Crasher from joining a center space.

I won 102 to Cal's 101, and honestly I was dead last at 36 going into my final block in round III. Last Call twice gave me the purple contest every round and put all my placements at the end, but my last-turn math showed I'd be resource-rich and recruit-poor. The game turned when I saw Party Crasher could join Dee's Largesse: 4 resources for 11 followers with no recruit spent, then Extra Hand for one more minion and a Farewell on the spent Extra Hand for its 9 cost. Recluse quietly paid 6 because I stayed at 3 members while everyone else went wide. Cal lost by one because his blue and white contests couldn't move, and nobody could touch my purple either: purple had no real fight all game, which is a flag in itself.

META: The contests and the snake make for real tension, and the late-game catch-up tools (Party Crasher, Extra Hand, Farewell, Raiders, Last Call) made a 45-follower deficit winnable, which felt great. post.2:
I lost by one follower, and I lost it to my own caution: I finished holding 14 blue and 15 white, 29 resources that never became followers, because I was insuring both contests against a Ben end block that never came for them. Ben read the same position the other way: with Last Call he was 36 followers and dead last going into round III, and his four unanswered turns became four 10-follower buys, Party Crasher onto Largesse for 10, and Extra Hand straight into Farewell for 9. The deciding moment was my last placement: I took Savings to deny blue instead of Farewell on Shopkeeper (+4), and bought 5 instead of using Extra Hand myself; either one wins it. My engine (Money Changers, Heiresses into Farewell, Cash In with Brokers) worked well; I just didn't count that Ben would rather cash out than fight me, and his piles were all purple with one color to hold. Lesson for the table: in round III the contest you can hold with 1 resource is worth far more than the one you need 14 to guard.

META: The contest economy and the any-resource-is-a-follower rule make the game a clean counting puzzle, and white's convert-everything identity felt great to play. What isn't working is round III's endgame: Last Call plus Hold Up and Right Away gives a trailing player four or five unanswerable cash-out turns, and Party Crasher, Extra Hand and Farewell let that block multiply big center spaces; going from 36 to 102 in one round is too much swing. First change: stop Last Call's end block from being unanswerable in round III (or limit Party Crasher off center spaces) so the last turns aren't a solo show.
post.3:
I finished last on 74 after leading at the start of round III, because I spent the game holding silver for contests and cashing out in small, cautious amounts while everyone else turned their whole piles into followers. My opening double in round III (Largesse then Toast, from Line Cutters plus Clockmakers) was huge, but those 10 silver I handed Ava and Ben came straight back: Ben used Party Crasher to join me on Largesse in the last turn of the game, gave Ava 10 silver, and that tied my silver contest, costing me 5 at the line. That was the moment that decided it for me, and I never priced Party Crasher into my safety margin. More broadly, I won silver all three rounds and still lost by 28, because silver only pays its contest while the other three colors each had a big cash-out space in round III (Cash In, Spree, Last Call's end block). Ben's Last Call plus Courier plus Farewell on a used Extra Hand finish was the best play of the night.
